In [[mathematics]], in the field of [[complex geometry]], a '''holomorphic curve''' in a [[complex manifold]] ''M'' is a non-constant [[holomorphic map]] ''f'' from the [[complex plane]] to ''M''.<ref name=Shiffman>{{harvtxt|Shiffman|1977}}, p.553</ref>

[[Nevanlinna theory]] addresses the question of the distribution  of values of a holomorphic curve in the complex [[projective line]].<ref name=Shiffman/><ref>{{cite book | author=Min Ru | title=Nevanlinna Theory and its Relation to Diophantine Approximation | publisher=World Scientific | isbn=981-02-4402-9 | year=2001 }}</ref>
